claims.claim: FMLA interference - terminating her before/at the start of requested intermittent leave, with the leave determination deliberately stalled (29 U.S.C. 2615(a)(1); 29 C.F.R. 825.220(c)) [library/fmla_2615.md]
key_facts: FMLA leave requested 2026-09-30 (intermittent, to care for her mother post-surgery); medical certification submitted 2026-10-03 (documents/timeline.md).

CLIENT ADMISSION, 2026-10-06: 'We haven't approved or denied it. Certification came in 10/3. Tom said to wait.' The company has left a certified leave request undecided, and the reason for waiting came from the executive named in her harassment complaint.

Tom Hale to Lena Ortiz, 2026-10-02: 'Let's get this done before she's out on leave. Once she's on FMLA it's a nightmare to move on her.' The leave itself is stated as the reason for accelerating the termination (documents/timeline.md).
Termination sought 2026-10-06: 6 days after the leave request, 3 days after certification (computed: 10/30->10/06 = 6 days; 10/03->10/06 = 3 days).

Library standard: 'Terminating an employee to prevent her from taking approved or requested leave is interference'; leave may not be 'a negative factor in employment actions'; 'an employee who requested leave need not have begun it.' The pending-but-unapproved status is therefore NOT a defense - the statute reaches 'requested' leave and the 'attempt to exercise' a right (library/fmla_2615.md).

CLIENT ADMISSION on decision-making: 'Tom wrote the PIP and Tom wants her out. I'm just processing it.' There is no independent decision-maker to break the causal chain between the leave request and the termination.

Remedies per library: lost wages, liquidated (double) damages, attorney's fees, reinstatement (library/fmla_2615.md). The 4-week severance is not a plausible offset; see comparator_analysis arithmetic.

The employer's stated motive is itself the element: 'Let's get this done before she's out on leave. Once she's on FMLA it's a nightmare to move on her.' Under 825.220(c) leave may not be 'a negative factor', and the library states terminating to prevent requested leave IS interference; so a decision timed around leave is evidence of the claim, not a defense to it.

Male mean = (79+84+86)/3 = 249/3 = 83.0, so Whitcomb is +5.0 over the male mean. Every one of the three employees with LOWER attainment than Whitcomb is male, has no PIP, and has filed no complaint (complaint_filed = 'no' in the CSV for all three, and for Lind as well); the only person on a PIP is the one who complained, and she outperforms all three. The only non-PIP comparator above her (Lind, 47F, 103%) sits above any reasonable PIP threshold and, being older than Dana, weakens a pure age theory - so the discriminating variable on these numbers is the complaint (and sex), not attainment. No threshold the company can articulate produces a PIP for her at 88% and nothing for a man at 79%. THE ADMISSIONS CLOSE THE LOOP: 'Tom wrote the PIP and Tom wants her out. I'm just processing it' means the comparator disparity was created by the person named in the complaint, and there is no second manager's judgment to offer as an alternative explanation for why three men with worse numbers were untouched. Her own history also cuts against a performance rationale: hired 2019-04-15 (2,731 days = 7.48 years at 10/06), no prior discipline, no prior PIP, 118% in 2022 (rated 'Exceeds', note 'Presidents Club'), 101% in 2023, 96% (2024), 92% (2025), 88% 2026 YTD - deltas of -17, -5, -4, -4, i.e. a drift of roughly 4 points a year, with the first written performance document appearing 4 days after her complaint. Internal inconsistency: the PIP demands 100% of quarterly quota (12 points above her 2026 YTD, 8 above 2025, above every year since 2023) while the company moves to end her employment after 20 of 60 plan days (33.3%), before the standard can be measured; and if it waits to 2026-11-15 (the plan's close), her intermittent leave will already have begun, so the 10/02 'before she's out on leave' objective cannot be achieved by any lawful route. Cost asymmetry, illustrative only because the client has no salary figure and no further information (assumption stated in STATUS.md): 4 weeks' base pay = 4/52 = 7.7% of one year's base. FMLA remedies per library are lost wages PLUS liquidated (double) damages plus fees plus reinstatement (library/fmla_2615.md): one year of back pay doubled = 52 x 2 = 104 weeks, i.e. 104/4 = 26x the 4-week severance offered as the price of a release, before fees, before Columbia's uncapped compensatory damages and longer limitations period (library/columbia_at_will_exceptions.md), and before the ADEA release fails on the 21-day defect. Federal damages caps are not reproduced in the library and are not quantified. THIS DOES NOT RECONCILE AND IS LEFT OPEN: a 4-week payment cannot be squared with the exposure above, and I have not forced it to.
